newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain denies talks with ETA may be on the cards.
newsitem.headline: Spain denies talks with ETA may be on the cards.

text.p: The Spanish government denied on Friday it was in talks with the Basque separatist group ETA and rejected a reported overture for peace negotiations.

"The government has not been in talks (with ETA), nor does it favour any type of indirect dialogue because it believes (ETA) could not create the appropriate conditions," Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja told reporters at a news conference following the weekly cabinet meeting.
Spanish daily ABC said on Friday moderate Basque leader Javier Arzallus had told Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar the government would soon receive an official offer from ETA to negotiate.
The spokesman for the Basque National Party, Inaki Anasagasti, later denied Arzallus had made such comments.

But in reply to a question concerning the newspaper report, Mayor Oreja told reporters the government had not established any type of dialogue with ETA and would not be willing to hold talks with a group that continued to kill and kidnap.
"ETA proves every day that it wants to continue kidnapping and killing," Mayor Oreja said.
The separatist group are currently holding a prison officer who was abducted 10 months ago. A Basque businessman missing since last week is also presumed kidnapped by ETA.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) have killed nearly 800 people in a drive for full independence which began in 1968.
